The provided text offers a brief but powerful reflection on George Orwell’s *1984*, highlighting the reader's sense of disturbance and awe at the author's prescient vision of a surveillance state. I find this perspective compelling because it underscores the enduring relevance of Orwell’s warnings about totalitarianism, suggesting that his fictional dystopia continues to resonate with contemporary global anxieties. It is striking how a novel written decades ago can still feel "all too real," serving as a chilling mirror to current societal trends.

The name of the river that runs through London is the Thames.
